status_observed: 500 {"detail":"Internal server error"} â€” and the contact is NOT deleted
what_is_wrong: Deleting a customer contact that is referenced by a customer activity (activities.related_contact_id) raises an unhandled DB FK/RESTRICT error and returns 500. The delete silently fails and the contact remains. delete_contact calls `await db.delete(row); await db.commit()` with no try/except, unlike its sibling update_contact (customers.py:453-457) which wraps commit in `except DBAPIError` and converts it to a client error. The vendor module handles the equivalent case correctly (DELETE /vendors/{id} on a vendor with usage returns a clean 409 "This vendor has usage history â€” deactivate instead of deleting"); the contact endpoint has no such guard.

status_observed: 200, but the stale_days threshold is ignored for every opportunity that has no activity logged
what_is_wrong: The `stale_days` filter returns the identical row set for every value from 0 to 99999. The WHERE clause is `stage NOT IN (WON,LOST) AND (last_activity_at IS NULL OR last_activity_at < cutoff)`. Because the IS NULL branch is unconditional, any open opportunity that has never had an activity logged matches at every threshold â€” so `stale_days=99999` ("no activity in the last 273 years") returns opportunities created two days ago. The day threshold only filters rows that already have a last_activity_at, making the filter effectively "open opportunities with no recent activity OR no activity at all, regardless of N". The correct behaviour for the NULL case is to fall back to created_at against the same cutoff. The same helper backs GET /api/v1/opportunities/summary/by-stage, so the stage counts and pipeline totals inherit the same wrong row set whenever stale_days is applied.
evidence:
Sweeping the threshold across five orders of magnitude returns the same 5 rows:
GET /api/v1/opportunities?stale_days=0      -> 200, n=5
GET /api/v1/opportunities?stale_days=1      -> 200, n=5
GET /api/v1/opportunities?stale_days=7      -> 200, n=5
GET /api/v1/opportunities?stale_days=365    -> 200, n=5
GET /api/v1/opportunities?stale_days=3650   -> 200, n=5
GET /api/v1/opportunities?stale_days=99999  -> 200, n=5
Identical titles every time: ['Deal Zenith','Deal Zenith','Deal Zenith','Stage9 Scoping Test Deal','ZZ Live Test Opportunity'] â€” exactly the 5 non-WON/non-LOST rows, all with last_activity_at=null.

Proof the threshold works only once last_activity_at is populated. I logged one activity on my own opportunity b5328d82-99b4-434d-9bf8-b0e2c1becece:
POST /api/v1/opportunities/b5328d82-.../activities {"activity_type":"CALL","activity_date":"2026-08-26","description":"ZZ live test opportunity activity"} -> 201
GET /api/v1/opportunities/b5328d82-... -> last_activity_at = "2026-08-26T06:52:51.797849"

After that, the same sweep:
stale_days=0     -> n=5, includes b5328d82 = True
stale_days=1     -> n=4, includes b5328d82 = False
stale_days=3650  -> n=4, includes b5328d82 = False
stale_days=99999 -> n=4, includes b5328d82 = False
The remaining 4 (last_activity_at=null) are still returned at stale_days=99999. 'Stage9 Scoping Test Deal' has created_at 2026-08-24T13:24:28, i.e. 2 days before the server date of 2026-08-26, yet it is reported as stale for 99999 days.

status_observed: 200; reference_number is a raw UUID on every EXPENSE row while PURCHASE_BILL rows carry a real code
what_is_wrong: EXPENSE rows return the expense row's own primary key as `reference_number` (e.g. '935ec148-831e-4dd3-b94c-a83b77762946'), whereas PURCHASE_BILL rows return a real document code ('PB-2028-0009'). The `search` query param is documented as 'Matches Reference Number', so a user cannot find an expense row by anything they can actually read on screen â€” searching works only for purchase bills. What I could not prove in this pass: whether this is intended. I checked the models and neither ExpenseClaim nor CompanyExpense has a human-facing code/number column, so there may be no display code to emit and this could be a deliberate fallback rather than a defect. Confirming requires a product decision on whether expenses should carry a generated code, which I could not determine from the API alone.
